title: Sheaf evaluation and sections-tensor maps for the point model
statement: In the ordinary point-extension models [def-pod-point-derived-hom-models], assume the explicit adjunction formula. For every module complex c and sheaf-module complex I, put P=Lc and H=Hom_B(P,I). There exist chain maps e_B:Tot(P tensor_B H) to I and beta:Tot(c tensor_R sections H) to sections Tot(P tensor_B H). Their homogeneous formulas are e_B(y tensor h)=(-1)^(pj)h_p(y) and beta(x tensor h)=(1 tensor x) tensor h. The tensor insertions, Hom evaluation and extension generator are the concrete ones of the cited models. No Hom comparison q, exactness, flatness, or injectivity is assumed; in particular this conclusion does not assert the evaluation square.

source.place: Tags 0A8X, 08J7: Hom complexes and ordinary internal Hom

proof.text: The presheaf tensor-Hom counit gives degreewise sheaf evaluation, multiplied in bidegree (p,j) by (-1)^(pj). Descend it through module sheafification and assemble via the total coproduct. Expand the Hom projection differential to verify the chain identity: the two terms with h(dy) cancel, leaving d_I h(y).

source.place: Tags 0A8X, 08J7: Hom complexes and ordinary internal Hom

proof.text: The explicit adjunction identifies its unit on x with 1 tensor x. Pair this with a section h using the ordinary sheaf tensor pairing and insert in the (p,j) total summand. Scalar balancing gives a map on the R-module tensor, and coproduct descent defines beta. Naturality of the unit and the two total differential terms prove its chain identity. No preservation of coproducts by sections is used. The formulas follow from the constructions.
